policy: Classify exact DCS types using powered chassis plus matching model evidence, or documented separate transport. Stationary deployment alone proves neither fixed infrastructure nor transportability. Towed also covers equipment packed as vehicle cargo, with one included tractor per piece. No type gains can_tow and no transit-defence whitelist changes. STATIC-chassis trucks without propulsion overrides remain unknown. Native mission movement/fire/recovery probes were not run.

The exact catalog type is the German Flakscheinwerfer 37. Primary wartime US documentation identifies the 150 cm heavy searchlight and its generator as individually transported on detachable four-wheel trailers towed by trucks. Official DCS product documentation identifies the included Siemens Flakscheinwerfer 37 and generator.

sources.summary: Official DCS WWII Assets Pack product list identifies Siemens Flakscheinwerfer 37 and generator among support units.

Primary US Military Intelligence Service Special Series 10, German Antiaircraft Artillery, February 1943, chapter 9(a)(2) Mobility: the heavy searchlight and generator each mount on a detachable four-wheel trailer towed by a truck (transcription line 16).

Fortification-history reproduction attributed to the Koblenz military technical collection, 150 cm Flakscheinwerfer 34/37 section (lines 99-103): the searchlight and associated Maschinensatz 33/37 use Sd.Ah. 102, later Sd.Ah. 104 transport trailers. Corroborates the named model rather than an unspecified searchlight.
